sources.note: Describes the sister pidgin (Yimas-Arafundi, yima1244), not the target. Sec. 2 only mentions the target: 'still another Yimas-lexified pidgin was used in trading contacts with Karawari speakers (Williams 2000)'. Sec. 4 Phonology gives 4 vowels and 15-16 consonants for Yimas-Arafundi Pidgin; no statement on stress or accent anywhere (zero hits for 'stress'/'accent').
